screening_decisions.reason: Mathematical modeling study estimating required sensitivity of hypothetical POC tests; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study with real patient data, does not verify performance against NAAT in a prospective clinical cohort, and does not present 2×2 data.
Meta-epidemiological study of prostate cancer bone metastases using healthcare claims data; wrong topic (not C. trachomatis), not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test.

Prospective trial component enrolled 1,384 female STD clinic patients and evaluated POC optical immunoassay (OIA) and DFA against PCR (NAAT) and cell culture. All participants received both index (POC) and reference (PCR) tests. While the abstract emphasizes decision-analysis outcomes, the underlying design is a paired diagnostic accuracy comparison of a rapid POC test versus a NAAT reference standard in a relevant clinical population.

Pilot study evaluating the QuickVue rapid diagnostic test against PCR for endocervical samples, reporting sensitivity and specificity. It is a diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test versus a NAAT reference standard in women. Abstract lacks explicit detail on prospective enrollment and consecutive sampling, but core design and population fit the review scope.
Clinical practice guideline for syndromic management; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study and does not evaluate a rapid POC test against NAAT.
Commentary and perspective article discussing ASSURED criteria and future STI diagnostics; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study with patient-level data and 2×2 results.

Prospective field study evaluating two chlamydia POC tests (CRT and ACON) against a gold-standard NAAT in 226 men and 225 women in Vanuatu. Reports sensitivity and specificity by sex. Study design, population, index test (rapid POC), reference standard (NAAT), and clinical setting all match the selection criteria.

Clinic-based evaluation of the Clearview Chlamydia MF rapid test against Roche Amplicor NAAT in 1,497 women, with all participants receiving both index and reference tests. Reports sensitivity, specificity, and PPV. Some participants were recruited from re-education centres rather than primary/secondary care facilities, introducing uncertainty about full adherence to the setting criterion; retained under the conservative instruction to include when in doubt.

Prospective cohort study evaluating a rapid urine test against PCR (NAAT) in 1,211 men attending sexual health and GUM clinics. Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV. Clearly a diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test versus NAAT reference standard in the target population (men at reproductive age).
CDC recommendations and guidance on laboratory-based detection methods; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test.
Systematic review of POC tests for multiple STIs; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Summary of evidence for CDC treatment guidelines; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Decision-tree and cost-effectiveness modeling study using a hypothetical cohort of 10,000 women; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study with real, prospectively enrolled participants and observed 2×2 data.

Evaluation of a CE-marked home-use test (HandiLab-C), not a rapid point-of-care test intended for immediate clinical decision-making during a healthcare encounter. The review scope is limited to POC testing in primary/secondary care settings; home tests fall outside this intervention definition.
Cochrane review of macrolide treatment for Haemophilus ducreyi (chancroid); wrong organism, wrong intervention (treatment, not diagnosis), and not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Methodological paper introducing the QUADAS-2 quality assessment tool; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test for C. trachomatis.
Methodological paper on bivariate meta-analysis for diagnostic reviews; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Systematic review of systematic reviews on CT POC tests; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Individual-based mathematical modeling study of partner notification strategies; not a diagnostic accuracy study.

Cross-sectional study determining prevalence and evaluating Clearview Chlamydia MF and CRT rapid tests against PCR in women at clinic settings (social hygiene and OB-GYN clinics). Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV. Core design is diagnostic accuracy of rapid tests versus NAAT. Abstract lacks explicit mention of prospective enrollment, consecutive sampling, and explicit 2×2 tables, but meets the scope conservatively.
Methodological study evaluating statistical tests for publication bias in diagnostic meta-analyses; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Interpretive review of RCTs evaluating chlamydia screening to prevent PID; not a diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test against NAAT.
Cohort study examining risk factors for CT-associated PID; not a diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test.
Methodological paper on applying GRADE to diagnostic test recommendations; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test for C. trachomatis.
Narrative review of laboratory diagnostic methods for CT; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a systematic review of clinical effectiveness and cost-effectiveness, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study presenting original 2×2 data comparing a rapid POC test against NAAT.
This is a systematic review of NAAT performance on urine versus traditional samples; it is not a primary study evaluating a rapid POC test against NAAT.
Evaluates Biostar Chlamydia OIA but uses a composite reference standard (positivity by two or more of culture, DFA, PCR, and OIA) rather than NAAT alone as required by the protocol.
National population-based prevalence survey of STIs; no rapid POC test was evaluated against a reference standard, so it is not a diagnostic accuracy study.

Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating rapid POC tests (ACON CT, QuickVue Chlamydia RT) against NAAT in symptomatic nonpregnant women of reproductive age using sequential sampling. Reports sensitivity and specificity consistent with 2×2 data.
Compares multiple assays using a composite reference standard (≥3 assays positive) rather than NAAT alone; does not meet the protocol requirement for NAAT as the reference standard.
Diagnostic accuracy study of rapid BioStar Chlamydia OIA against two different NAATs in adolescent (reproductive age) women. Reports sensitivity and specificity (2×2 data) and meets all key criteria.
Diagnostic accuracy study of Chlamydia Rapid Test Device versus BD ProbeTec ET PCR (NAAT) in asymptomatic men of reproductive age. Reports sensitivity and specificity with prospective enrollment.
Prevalence study using PCR only; no rapid POC test evaluated as an index test against a reference standard.
Narrative review of laboratory diagnostic methods; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study presenting original 2×2 data.
Sentinel surveillance cross-sectional study measuring STI/HIV prevalence and risk behaviors; not a diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test.
Cross-sectional prevalence and etiology study of lower genital tract infections; no evaluation of rapid POC test diagnostic accuracy against NAAT.
Clinic-based diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid POC test versus PCR in nonpregnant women at reproductive age attending STI clinics. Reports sensitivity and specificity.
General review article discussing diagnostic tests; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study with original 2×2 data.

Performance evaluation study of Chlamydia Rapid Test versus PCR and strand displacement amplification (NAATs) using self-collected vaginal swabs in women aged 16–54. Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV (2×2 data).
Study of C. trachomatis serovar distributions and symptom associations; no rapid POC test diagnostic accuracy evaluation.
Performance evaluation of CRT POC test versus Aptima NAAT in women at STI clinics. Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV against a NAAT reference standard.
Review article on immune response mechanisms and infertility; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Methodological paper on search strategies for diagnostic accuracy studies; not a primary clinical study presenting patient-level 2×2 data.
Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study comparing rapid OIA to LCR (a NAAT) in outpatient clinic attendees. Reports sensitivity and specificity, meeting the protocol requirements.
Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating three POC tests against NAAT in women attending an STI clinic. Reports sensitivities against the NAAT gold standard in the target population.
Review of risk factors for genital chlamydial infection; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Laboratory guidelines document; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study presenting original 2×2 data.

Diagnostic accuracy/feasibility study comparing a prototype POC device to cervical NAAT in adolescent women. Reports sensitivity and specificity, meeting the core inclusion criteria despite small sample sizes during prototype refinement.
Retrospective chart review evaluating treatment follow-up after positive screening tests; not a diagnostic accuracy study of rapid POC test performance against NAAT.
